text: This Motion seeks authorization to release $15,000 in Section 45(9) funds to Heritage Toronto for two heritage plaques to recognize both the heritage and cultural significance of City Park Co-op in the Church Wellesley Village. City Park was the first Modern, multi-building apartment complex in Toronto and, at the time of its construction in 1954, the biggest single residential project in the country. The buildings, designed by architect Peter Caspari, replaced a block of housing considered substandard during a post-war push to improve living conditions in the City. Caspari’s City Park, located between Church, Wood, and Alexander streets, consisted of three, 14-storey buildings with large open spaces between each one, which allowed more light to reach individual units. The architect also paid particular attention to eliminating sound transfer between apartments: each unit is separated…

City Council on November 25 and 26, 2020, adopted the following: 1. City Council increase the Approved 2020 Operating Budget for Heritage Toronto on a one-time basis by $15,000.00 gross, $0 net, fully funded by Section 45(9) community benefits obtained from the development at 608-618 Yonge Street, 5-9 St Joseph Street and 15-25 St. Nicholas Street (Source Account: XR3028- 4500108) for the production and installation of two heritage plaques at City Park Co-op (484 Church Street, 31 Alexander Street, and 51 Alexander Street).
